sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Roopesh Kumar Mishra Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Abrar Ahmad Siddiqui Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
2. Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

3. Heard Shri Roopesh Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant and Shri Abrar Ahmad,
learned counsel for the informant as well as Shri R.P. Patel, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
4. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.248 of 2022, under Sections 376, 366 and 342 I.P.C., Police Station Kaundhiyara, District Prayagraj, during the pendency of trial.

5. As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have enticed away the informant on 22.08.2022 between 4-5 am and had taken her in a Tavera vehicle to Rewa, Madhya Pradesh from Anurag Shukla @ Prince vs State Of U.P. on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70626145/
1 where he alongwith victim is stated to have gone to Surat, Gujarat whereby they are stated to have entered into physical relationship.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.

entities.text: Anurag Shukla @ Prince vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The FIR is delayed by about two and half months and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

The victim is a consenting party as is clearly evident from her statement recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C. whereby she has categorically stated that she did not raise any alarm at the time of physical relationship with the applicant and also she had not whispered a single word during the said sojourn all the way to Surat, Gujarat.
Learned counsel has further stated that the FIR is an afterthought and has been instituted after legal consultation and deliberations.
Learned counsel has also filed the letter which is purported to have been written by the informant/victim to the applicant.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.

The circumstances which,
as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
The criminal history assigned to the applicant has been explained.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 08.11.2022.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the victim was suffering from depression as such, is not lodged the FIR in time, although they could not produce any document in support of the said averments.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, taking into consideration the fact that there is an inordinate delay in lodging the FIR and the fact that the victim is major more than 20 years of age, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant- Anurag Shukla @ Prince involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii). The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
(iv) The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected of the commission of which he is suspected.

(v) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the Anurag Shukla @ Prince vs State Of U.P. on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70626145/
2 evidence.
10.

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
11.

It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
